incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: multi-region GPU quota hit -> autoscaler stall (4260001234)
incident-bot: Severity: P1, channel: #incidents, pager: @Anna (oncall)
Anna (oncall): I'm seeing autoscaler alerts: scale-up requests failing with 'quotaExceeded' across us-west3 and us-east1. Queue depth trending up.
Mike (sre): Confirming. Queue length for gen workers spiked from ~200 to 2.6k in 6m, avg latency up 4x. Errors show provisioning failures repeatedly.
Raj (infra): GCP quotas for GPUs in us-west3 show near 100% usage; AWS fallback region (us-west-2) also hitting account service-quotas due to other bursts. Looks like we got a fanout: traffic routed to multiple regions and all hit soft caps.
Elaine (support): Customer impact: a few high-traffic customers report 5xx on generate endpoints. Escalated tickets from Acme and BlueWave. They report timeouts ~30s then 502s.
Sam (product): Which customers are on Dedicated vs Hosted? Any reserved capacity we can borrow?
Julie (customer-ops): Acme is Hosted standard tier, BlueWave on Dedicated but burst mode enabled. No reserved spare capacity available in their Dedicated pools.
Anna (oncall): Initial mitigation plan: 1) Pause non-critical batch jobs; 2) Route new sessions to lower-capacity model variants; 3) Try cross-region fallback to ap-northeast1 if capacity available; 4) Engage cloud quota support for emergency bump. I'll coordinate.
Mike (sre): Doing 1 and 2 now. Pausing scheduled embedding jobs in infra namespace: `kubectl -n infra scale --replicas=0 cronjob/embeddings-batch`
k8s-bot: cronjob/embeddings-batch scaled to 0 replicas.
Mike (sre): pausing non-critical batch consumers on gen-pool-prod. Also lowering continuous-batch window to reduce token churn.
Raj (infra): Running quick quota checks. GCP: ```gcloud compute regions describe us-west3 --format=\"json(quotas)\" | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric==\"GPUS\")'``` shows limit 64, usage 64. us-east1 limit 128 usage 124 (spiky). AWS: `aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code elastic-inference --quota-code L-XXXX` returning near max in us-west-2.
Anna (oncall): Trying model fallback routing to smaller variants (quantized/reduced-context). If model switch successful, should cut reqs/sec and token-per-request by ~30-50%.
Mike (sre): Implemented routing rule: if queue > 500, route to model:redwood-q4-8k-50q. Patching rollout now.
Sam (product): Heads up: fallback model reduces quality for some prompts — notify support to set expectations.
Elaine (support): Messaging ready: "We're routing traffic to a lower-capacity model to maintain availability; you may see minor quality differences." Sending to Acme/BlueWave.
Raj (infra): I can try spinning up smaller GPU shapes that don't count against the same quota (e.g., switch from A100 regional quota to T4 family). Trying `gcloud compute instances create --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 ... --region=us-west3` but last retries failing with quotaExceeded for GPUs overall.
Mike (sre): Can we fallback to CPU-only endpoints for low-priority requests? Queue-priority gating: drop best-effort on CPU to preserve GPU for interactive sessions.
Anna (oncall): Implementing priority gating: requests with header `x-request-priority: low` get CPU-only route. Patching envoy config.
Mike (sre): Patch applied. CPU workers scaling up slowly — still limited by nodepool quotas but helps reduce GPU demand ~12%.
Julie (customer-ops): Customer impact update: Acme reports partial recovery of interactive flows after model fallback. BlueWave still seeing queued jobs.
Raj (infra): Reached out to GCP support with ticket 123456789 — asked for temporary quota increase for GPUs in us-west3 and us-east1 (emergency). ETA unknown but marked as priority.
Anna (oncall): While we wait, I'm proposing traffic steering: shift new session allocations away from us-west3 to ap-northeast1 and europe-west1 if capacity exists. Mike, can autoscaler routing rules be updated quickly?
Mike (sre): Yes. Adjusted smart routing policy to prefer regions with spare capacity. Deploying now.
Mike (sre): `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routing -d '{\"policy\":\"prefer-region\",\"regions\":[\"ap-northeast1\",\"europe-west1\"],\"threshold\":500}'` (applied)
k8s-bot: routing policy applied, live in 30s.
Anna (oncall): Observability: token-level cost+latency dashboard shows drop in us-west3 token consumption after routing change. Queue depth plateauing at ~800 instead of 2.6k. Latency trending down but still above SLO.
Sam (product): Need a customer-facing summary for the status page and PSR. Draft: "We experienced GPU capacity exhaustion affecting provisioning in multiple regions which caused scale-up to stall. Traffic was rerouted and lower-capacity model variants used to restore availability. We're working with cloud providers to secure capacity and will follow up with timeline." Approve?
Elaine (support): Approve. Adding note about targeted customers impacted and mitigation steps.
Anna (oncall): Next steps: - Continue routing and priority gating. - Monitor quotas while cloud support works ticket. - Prepare on-call handoff in 3 hours. Do we have an ETA on vendor reply?
Raj (infra): GCP acknowledged; initial reply says they elevated to quota team, may take 2-4 hours for emergency provisioning. AWS case opened too, same window.
Mike (sre): We're also preparing a runbook for long tail: if quotas can't be raised quickly, we'll: 1) enforce stronger priority gating (interactive-only GPUs), 2) enable a temporary rate-limit per-customer, 3) open a sales/CS-assisted communication for high-value customers to offer dedicated reserved capacity options.
Julie (customer-ops): I'll coordinate CS outreach and offer temporary credits or prioritized support to impacted accounts.
Sam (product): Can we schedule a follow-up postmortem and quantify cost of emergency region usage / fallback model quality? We'll need that for the PSR.
Anna (oncall): Agreed. I'll create a follow-up doc and invite SRE, Infra, Product, Support.
Mike (sre): Quick log snippets showing provisioning failure: ```Provisioner: request id=0x4f3a; region=us-west3; error=quotaExceeded: requested 8 GPUs, available 0```
Anna (oncall): tagging for handoff: @Mike (sre) will lead the next shift, @Raj (infra) remains on vendor ticket, @Sam (product) will own customer comms, @Elaine (support) will track open tickets. I'm going offline for 20m but will reconvene in 30.
k8s-bot: autoscaler alert suppressed for 30m by Anna (oncall).
Elaine (support): Sent status update to affected customers; Acme confirmed degraded quality but acceptable for now.
Mike (sre): Current status (4260004988): queue size 730, interactive latency down 35%, provisioning errors reduced but still occasional quotaDenied responses. Cloud vendor working ticket.
Anna (oncall): Handoff note: incident is stabilized but not fully resolved. On-call followup required until vendor grants quota or we procure dedicated capacity. Please continue monitoring dashboards and escalate if queue > 1000 or errors spike.
Julie (customer-ops): Logging PSR invite and noting impacted accounts for follow-up.
Sam (product): Thanks all. We'll prepare a post-incident review once quota status is final.
incident-bot: Incident 4260001234 moved to 'stabilized' state, P1 -> monitoring."
